newsitem.title: USA: Clinton turns to friend Slater for Transport post.
newsitem.headline: Clinton turns to friend Slater for Transport post.

text.p: Rodney Slater's road to nomination as transportation secretary began in Arkansas and a friendship with Bill Clinton.

A long-time political ally of the president, Slater, 41, was rewarded for his support of then-governor Clinton by being appointed to the Arkansas Highway Commission -- later becoming the first black to serve as its chairman.
When Clinton came to Washington, he had another job for Slater, making him head of the Federal Highway Administration, which oversees the nation's sprawling highway system.
Since becoming administrator in 1993, Slater has travelled more than 300,000 miles and visited 40 states carrying out his mission, according to his office.
The highway administration is an agency within the Transportation Department that Clinton now wants him to head -- replacing Federico Pena, whom he chose as his new energy secretary.

If confirmed by the Senate, Slater would become the nation's top transportation official as the Republican-controlled Congress takes up debate on reauthorizatiing the Intermodel Surface Transportation Efficiency Act -- crucial in setting federal funding priorities.
A native of Marianna, Arkansas, Slater went to Eastern Michigan University on a football scholarship and graduated in 1977. He earned a law degree from the University of Arkansas in 1980.
Slater was vice president of governmental affairs for Arkansas State University when Clinton tapped him for the federal highway post.
Slater and his wife, Cassandra Wilkins, have one daughter, Bridgette.
